hints: Start from the target: $h$ must come out in $\text{J s}$, with $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m}$ and distance $D$ in $\text{m}$, energy $E$ in $\text{J}$ and velocity $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Rewrite $\text{J s}$ in base form as $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-1}$ so you can compare it with the combination $DE/v$ after cancelling $\text{m}$.
Form the unit product for $DE/v$ as $\text{m} \times \text{J} \div \text{m s}^{-1}$ and check the other options for $\text{s}^{-1}$, $\text{C N}^{-1}$ and $\text{m}^3 \text{s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough: Identify the homogeneity test: the right-hand side must simplify to the SI units of $h$, which are $\text{J s}$.
Recall $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2}$, so $\text{J s} = \text{kg m}^2 \text{ s}^{-1}$.
Check the units of $DE/v$: $D$ is $\text{m}$, $E$ is $\text{J}$, $v$ is $\text{m s}^{-1}$, so units are $\text{m} \times \text{J} / \text{m s}^{-1}$.
Simplify: $\text{m}$ cancels and $1/\text{s}^{-1} = \text{s}$, giving $\text{J s}$, exactly the units of $h$.
The other combinations give $\text{s}^{-1}$ for $v/D$, units involving coulombs and newtons for $1/4\pi E$, and $\text{m}^3 \text{ s}^{-2}$ for $Fr^2/m$. This is option A.

A.explanation: $DE/v$ has units $\text{m} \times \text{J} / \text{m s}^{-1} = \text{J s}$, which matches the units of $h$.

B.explanation: $v/D$ has units $\text{m s}^{-1}/\text{m} = \text{s}^{-1}$, which is frequency, not $\text{J s}$.

C.explanation: $1/E$ with $E$ as electric field strength in $\text{N C}^{-1}$ gives units $\text{C N}^{-1}$, not $\text{J s}$.
